title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
sub: Search the documents, give the closest passages to the model, and ask once.

steps.d:
"How long is the warranty on the DW-480,
and what voids it?"

steps.h: Your code turns the question into a vector
Your code takes the four closest passages
steps.d:
0.83  dw480-manual.md  §9 Warranty
0.79  dw480-manual.md  §9.2 Exclusions
0.61  dw300-manual.md  §8 Warranty
0.58  install-guide.md  §2

SYSTEM   Answer only from the sources. Cite them.
SOURCES  [1] … [4]
QUESTION How long is the warranty …

"Two years from delivery [1]. Void if installed
without the anti-tip bracket or run on a
generator without a line conditioner [2]."

climb: Move up when one search is not enough and the next search depends on the result of the last one. In this run RAG found two of the three exclusions and could not tell that one was missing.

use.p: If you have uploaded files to a chat app and asked questions about them, you have used RAG. The product searched your files for the passages closest to your question, gave them to the model, and asked once. It searches only once, so it cannot tell if the search missed something.

build.code:
q_vec  = embed(question)
chunks = store.search(q_vec, k=4)
prompt = render(SYSTEM, sources=chunks, question=question)
answer = model.complete(prompt)      # one call. your code chose every step.
